title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

errors: No mathematical errors. dy = a dx/√(2ax + x²) follows from C = D = βa. The logarithmic integral vanishes at x = 0, and s = √(2ax + x²) corresponds to E = 0.
Section numbering slip in the original: 'XXVIII' is used both on p. 399 and here. The next section on p. 401 is XXIX.

ideas.what: Sail curve under normal wind pressure ∝ cos²φ has constant tension and is a catenary with interchanged axes
ideas.where_published: E410 itself; the velaria was also treated in Euler's earlier mechanics writings (exact locus unsure)

ideas.what: Planar equilibrium of a rod with tension T, shear V, moment Vv; moment proportional to curvature; d(moment) = shear·ds
ideas.modern_name: Balance equations of a planar (Euler–Kirchhoff) inextensible rod including shear force
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, E410 (1771), as emphasized by Truesdell (1960); later generalized by Kirchhoff and Clebsch
ideas.where_published: E410 (Novi Comm. Petrop. 15); discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies 1638–1788 (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Statement of the elastica problem: a weightless uniform rod bent only by end forces

deep.surprise_reason: The velaria-as-catenary result is classical. The rod equations with shear force in E410 are well known and have been celebrated by Truesdell. Nothing on this page appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The printed text reads 'siue naturam curuae elasticae definire', with 'naturam' hyphenated as 'natu-ram' across the line break. The transcription is otherwise accurate.
The section number 'XXVIII' duplicates the one on p. 399. This is an error in the original print, not in the transcription.
